COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
27.12.2024 WPPIL No. 180 of 2024
Hon'ble G. Narendar, C.J.
Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Mr. Navnish Negi, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. Manoj Kumar, learned Standing Counsel for 
the Union of India- respondent no.1.
3. Mr. Amarendra Pratap Singh, learned Additional 
Advocate General assisted by Mr. S.S. Chaudhary, 
learned Brief Holder for the State.
4. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned 
counsel for the respondents, and Ms. Nitika
Khandelwal, Director, Urban Development Department.
5. Pursuant to the order of this Court dated 
26.12.2024, the Director, Urban Development 
Department was present virtually. She submits that 
there are various affordable housing schemes, and they 
have carried out a census of the number of rag-pickers, 
and about 740 rag-pickers have been identified and out 
of the same, about 549 rag-pickers have been issued 
identity cards and the Government would be taking 
further steps to make available to these identified 
persons the affordable housing schemes.
6. The fact remains that weather, in the coming 
couple of months, is in all likelihood going to be harsh  according to the forecast and mere availability of 
affordable housing schemes would not be an immediate 
succour to the homeless people. In order to protect 
them from the adverse weather conditions, this Court 
has proposed to the Director, Urban Development to 
explore the possibility of creating temporary housing 
facilities with a view to mitigate the hardships that the 
shelterless rag-pickers would be forced to face.
7. The Court has suggested creation of temporary 
dormitory accommodations with tents and necessary 
infrastructure like bedding and clothing till they are 
able to tide over the cold weather.
8. The Director, Urban Development has sought a 
week’s time to devise a proposal and place it before 
this Court for approval and implementation. The same 
is placed on record.
9. List this matter on 02.01.2025, at the same 
stage. 
 (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J) (G. Narendar, CJ)
 27.12.2024 27.12.2024
NISHANT

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
02.01.2025 WPPIL No. 180 of 2024
Hon'ble G. Narendar, C.J.
Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Mr. Navnish Negi, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. Manoj Kumar, learned Standing Counsel for 
the Union of India- respondent no.1.
3. Mr. C.S. Rawat, learned Chief Standing Counsel 
for the State.
4. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned 
Chief Standing Counsel for the State, and Ms. Nitika
Khandelwal, Director, Urban Development Department.
5. An action taken report dated 31.12.2024 has 
been filed in the Court along with the communication 
addressed to the Chief Standing Counsel and signed by 
the Director, Urban Development Department.
6. In Paragraph No.6 of the said report, it is stated 
that they have identified 1056 rag-pickers, and out of 
them, 40 rag-pickers were found to be homeless, and a 
total of 101 shelters/ Rain Basera are established by 
the ULBs’ and there are 48 permanent shelters/ Rain 
Baseras with a capacity to house and accommodate 
1268, and the Directorate has also setup 53 temporary 
shelters/ Rain Baseras with intake capacity of 935.
7. In Paragraph No.7, the number of homeless, who 
have been shifted to the Rain Baseras is set out. In  Paragraph No.8, it is stated that 452 bonfire/ Alao are 
stated to have been provided. In Paragraph No.9, it is 
stated that adequate number of blankets have been 
distributed, and in Paragraph No.10, it is stated that a 
sum of Rs.50.00 lakhs has been set apart for the 
purpose of maintenance of night shelters. In Paragraph 
No.11, it is stated that 45 health camps have been 
organized for the rag-pickers and boots, safety jackets 
and helmets have been provided to 151, 165 and 26 
rag-pickers respectively.
8. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that 
he has not been furnished a copy of the report dated 
31.12.2024.
9. We have queried learned counsel for the 
petitioner whether it would be possible for him to 
personally interact with the rag-pickers and place a 
report before this Court, to which, he has prayed for a 
week’s time.
10. The action taken report dated 31.12.2024 is 
placed on record.
11. It is further directed that the Department shall 
depute one officer to accompany the petitioner’s 
counsel and show him the camps where the rag-pickers 
are housed.
12. List this matter on 09.01.2025, at the same 
stage. 
 (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J) (G. Narendar, CJ)
 02.01.2025 02.01.2025
NISHANT

09.01.2025 WPPIL No. 180 of 2024 
Hon’ble G. Narendar, C.J.
Hon’ble Ashish Naithani, J. 
1. Mr. Navnish Negi, learned counsel for 
the petitioner. 
2. Mr. Manoj Kumar, learned Standing
Counsel for the Union of India. 
3. Mr. C.S. Rawat, learned Chief Standing
Counsel assisted by Mr. Gajendra Tripathi, 
learned Standing Counsel for the State. 
4. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner 
Mr. Navnish Negi, and the learned Chief 
Standing Counsel Mr. C.S. Rawat, and the 
Director Ms. Nitika Khandelwal, who has 
submitted to the Court that steps have been 
taken and instructions issued to have the 
rag-pickers examined medically and that 
there are proposals to make it a calendar 
event to ensure the health of these 
marginalized class of citizens. That apart, 
the Director has also submitted that 
instructions have been issued to ensure that 
sanitation facilities are provided to the rag￾pickers, and that such instructions have been 
issued to the local authorities. The same are 
placed on record. 
5. The Amicus Curiae after a field visit and  interaction with the rag-pickers has filed a 
detailed report. A copy of which is also 
furnished to the respondent Government. 
6. Having heard the Director, we are of the 
opinion that the submissions made and steps 
initiated by the Director would be better 
appreciated if it is placed before this Court in 
the form of an affidavit along with the 
enclosures. Along with such material, 
including communications, directions, 
instructions issued for ameliorating the lives 
of these marginalized citizens. 
7. Affidavit by tomorrow. 
8. List the matter on 10.01.2025. 
 
 (Ashish Naithani, J.) (G. Narendar, C.J.)
